25.explanation: The Kerala Assembly's resolution asked for 'Keralam' in the First Schedule and in all Eighth Schedule languages. Amending the First Schedule does not automatically amend the Eighth Schedule, and an Art. 3/4 law needs only a simple majority (Art. 4(2)).

26.explanation: State names are listed in the First Schedule, which Parliament amends under Arts. 3–4.

sources.title: Constitution of India, First Schedule; Article 4

27.explanation: Under the proviso to Art. 3, the President refers the bill to the State Legislature for its views, but those views do not bind Parliament.

28.explanation: Linguistic reorganisation on 1 November 1956 came through both the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956.

29.explanation: If the State does not give its views within the set time, the bill can still be introduced in Parliament.

30.explanation: 'Keralaputra' in Ashoka's Rock Edict II refers to the Chera kingdom.

31.explanation: The NTA is a society registered under the Societies Registration Act (2017), not a statutory body. It works under the Ministry of Education, and its governing body includes academics as well as officials.

32.explanation: The NTA was set up in 2017 as a society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.

33.explanation: Dr K. Radhakrishnan, who chaired the 2024 NTA reform committee, is a former ISRO Chairman.

34.explanation: The committee proposed 'DIGI-EXAM' identity verification modelled on DigiYatra.

sources.title: Radhakrishnan Committee report on NTA reforms (Oct 2024)

35.explanation: Education is in the Concurrent List (Entry 25, List III) since the 42nd Amendment.

sources.title: Constitution of India, Seventh Schedule List III

36.explanation: India imports about 85–88% of its crude, and prices above $100 feed imported inflation. High crude prices increase OMC under-recoveries rather than reducing them, so 3 is false.

37.explanation: Switzerland is India's largest gold import source, at roughly 40% of imports.

sources.title: Ministry of Commerce trade data (gold imports by country)

38.explanation: Mobilising idle household gold through monetisation schemes meets demand without fresh imports, easing the CAD.

39.explanation: Exiting FIIs sell rupee assets and buy dollars, so dollar demand rises and the rupee weakens.

40.explanation: The GMS mobilises idle gold, channels it into productive use and cuts imports. Forcing appreciation of the real effective exchange rate is not one of its aims.

41.explanation: India's forex reserves are foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position with the IMF.

42.explanation: The Bhojshala–Kamal Maula complex is in Dhar, Madhya Pradesh.

43.explanation: The Act freezes religious character as on 15 August 1947, and s.4(3)(a) exempts AMASR-protected ancient monuments. Bhojshala was protected long before 1991 (an ASI monument since the early 20th century), so 3 is wrong.

44.explanation: Paramara king Bhoja (c. 1010–1055 CE) founded Bhojshala as a centre of Sanskrit learning, and Vagdevi is Saraswati. The Chandelas were not linked to it.

45.explanation: Alexander Cunningham, first Director-General of the ASI (1861), is called the Father of the ASI.

46.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 swap Articles 25 and 26. Art. 29(1) protects language, script and culture, and Art. 30 gives all minorities (religious or linguistic) the right to run educational institutions.

47.explanation: Artemis II carried international CubeSats from Germany (TACHELES), South Korea (K-RadCube), Saudi Arabia and Argentina (ATENEA).

48.explanation: Artemis II is a crewed lunar flyby on a free-return trajectory, not a landing. It also flew the Orion Optical Communications System (O2O) laser link for high-rate video.

49.explanation: A free-return trajectory uses the Moon's gravity to swing the spacecraft back to Earth without a major engine burn.

50.explanation: Glover is the first person of colour, Koch the first woman and Hansen (CSA) the first non-American to travel beyond low Earth orbit. Artemis II does not land, so no one walks on the Moon and pair 2 is wrong.

51.explanation: AVATAR (A Virtual Astronaut Tissue Analog Response) uses organ-chips made from the crew's own cells to study deep-space effects.

sources.title: NASA: AVATAR experiment on Artemis II

52.explanation: The Soviet Luna 9 (February 1966) made the first soft landing on the Moon, showing the surface could support a lander. Surveyor 1 followed in June 1966.
